To import your ChatGPT memory and context into [Claude AI](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESTgHEIkXXUeLtwNc8dsULiQUZ6IulLjzsqCV4RTsoJ6mOUSrghRuUa5k_-hn5dcW60JwNMgqszyNbDwO4g1LvqVLpZ6kfN3Fa_ZGCnuS9dA), `use Claude's built-in memory import feature` to transfer your preferences, working style, and project details.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESiAEBxCJF159sLdH7OhqfMwY7fDsTlNxO0LHTMY9rl_ZCWMdIEL6f4IwQd0mZ_1hPa3_gOtHgZJsrZRxstd0Dp6qs9CW2I3qP7_g7tBWTvB5kn174r6KNYUueviLWFu-HzRB3kJhsK4av-uyyZKCbCQDnl_mMR6_M90-45n2tvdK6G2tXJ_NJVakl)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESvAEBxCJF1x0q-6JemXwRPf941TDF_spW9SJ_5Ft0X-P1YUziBSVUgVayNgN9bE4uPi9yd2vFinHmTMr6cZiwuTM60GpkYh87UfSfvoZGaOCwRIaaubTxaOvbjHlFC71WmcVrehUAdkWMh9KCFw3d72wt_9tZR20QFgkIjzXBD4v45Wc_DFmxmqGLk0iuAhdQ3VsfSKYSvURpT6HaAJ5Q_HD3NlpsaPe5rusB0A1hJWmYuHmNZzJYhLtly3fEaw)

### Steps to Import ChatGPT Memory into Claude

- **Open Claude Settings:** Log in to Claude, click your profile picture in the bottom-left corner, and select **Settings**.
- **Navigate to Capabilities:** Go to the **Capabilities** tab and find **Import memory from other AI providers** , then click **Start import**.
- **Copy the Prompt:** Claude will display a pre-written export prompt. Click to copy it.
- **Run the Prompt in ChatGPT:** Open ChatGPT in a new conversation (enable "thinking mode" or ensure your personalization and chat history references are turned on) and paste the prompt.
- **Transfer the Summary:** Copy ChatGPT's generated response summary.
- **Add to Claude Memory:** Return to Claude's import window, paste the summary into the field, and click **Add to memory**.[[1]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7R3ZIVF-c1I&vl=en)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESiAEBxCJF159sLdH7OhqfMwY7fDsTlNxO0LHTMY9rl_ZCWMdIEL6f4IwQd0mZ_1hPa3_gOtHgZJsrZRxstd0Dp6qs9CW2I3qP7_g7tBWTvB5kn174r6KNYUueviLWFu-HzRB3kJhsK4av-uyyZKCbCQDnl_mMR6_M90-45n2tvdK6G2tXJ_NJVakl)[[3]](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/qiTiOP_wrgM)

### Optional: Full Data & Chat History Export
If you want to transfer full conversation archives or custom instructions as project knowledge files rather than just long-term memory:

- Go to ChatGPT and request a full data export via **Settings > Data Controls > Export Data** (this can take 24–48 hours to arrive via email).
- Create a new project in Claude and upload the resulting JSON or exported markdown files as project knowledge.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESsgEBxCJF131Q-8KZJ3c6JEneSqvphA1OM0wTRvr_4wCmnK-F7fh138Ywk8pCFxzF8dyYoJOb4aG06I96myoE27cVsNej7XsI21u9G4QRPSOUDvRwpBxIrutrqenOTA4VKCxmSFE56kwEOFDkm6CPwb5T4_dGvbR1cfpeHFQtwI5f3v1bUGv4qECrD59llWNsygKVLsjs6kB8UPu_GuoVt6bW63FyhXhlbhIpXRDgjVIQmb7W)[[2]](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/jessramosmsba_everyone-is-switching-from-chatgpt-to-claude-activity-7433581153623834625-PSDU)[[3]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zbwNtv-Emog&t=12)[[4]](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/LP2N0tmPKoI)

You know that you can import your ChatGPT memory to Claude?

Claude or ChatGPT, they are about the same.

But how can you very simply switch from one to another, well turns out it takes a few steps.

So I wrote this free guide on how to switch from ChatGPT → to Claude or, Claude → to ChatGPT here: https://t.co/rvov3XYkqt

I'm sure there is someone around you who asked you this, this week: "I love the new GPT-6 Astra, but how do I switch from Claude to ChatGPT?"

Or maybe someone who has been using ChatGPT for personal questions, and want to get Claude only for their professional work. It also works.

I won't go into details here, I don't have enough characters to give you all of the steps, but it goes like this:

1. From ChatGPT to Claude.

✦ Settings → Privacy → Export data (pick 90 days).
✦ Get the zip from your email, unzip it.
✦ Open a new Claude chat, upload the files, paste my prompt. It turns your whole history + memories into ONE Markdown file: Claude-to-ChatGPT .md
✦ Upload that file to your ChatGPT Library, ask it to save it to memory.

If switching from Chat GPT to Claude feels like a breakup, don’t worry, I’ve got you. 📲

You can skip the whole relearning process in Claude with just one prompt. Comment CLAUDE for the exact prompt I used.
